original_question: Which chromosome carries the gene that is mutated in the rarely diagnosed syndrome caused by the dramatic overexpression of that gene and, accordingly, excessive levels of estrogens?

final_qi.question: Which chromosome carries the gene that is mutated in the rarely diagnosed syndrome caused by the dramatic overexpression of that gene and, accordingly, excessive levels of estrogens?
final_qi.long_answer: Aromatase excess syndrome is a very rare disorder in which activating or duplication mutations lead to marked over-expression of the aromatase gene (CYP19A1). The resulting increase in aromatase activity converts androgens to estrogens, producing abnormally high circulating estrogen levels. The CYP19A1 gene is situated at cytogenetic band 15q21.2 on chromosome 15; therefore, chromosome 15 is the chromosome that carries the gene mutated in this estrogen-excess syndrome.

0.question: Which syndrome is caused by the dramatic overexpression of a gene that leads to excessive levels of estrogens?

final_answer.long_answer: Aromatase excess syndrome is a rare disorder in which structural mutations (duplications, inversions, translocations) increase expression of the aromatase gene CYP19A1, producing abnormally high estrogen levels. The CYP19A1 gene is located on chromosome 15q21, so chromosome 15 is the chromosome that carries the mutated, over-expressed gene.

The CYP19A1 gene is located at 15q21.2, so the responsible gene—and therefore the syndrome-causing mutation—resides on chromosome 15.
